title: Displacement, Double Displacement and Redox Reactions

items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A rusty bicycle chain and a stale packet of namkeen open the lesson: **what in the air changes them?**

Iron nails in copper sulphate lead to **displacement**; two pairs of solutions swap ions in **double displacement**.

Heating copper, then passing hydrogen over it, shows **oxidation and reduction** together. The hook returns as **corrosion** and **rancidity**.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• writing and balancing equations with state symbols

• combination, decomposition, exothermic and endothermic reactions

• ions and their charges, e.g. $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Explain displacement using metal reactivity.

**2.** Explain double displacement and precipitation.

**3.** Identify oxidation, reduction, oxidising and reducing agents.

**4.** Explain corrosion and rancidity, and how to prevent them.

**5.** Give a reaction all the types it belongs to.

**What this shows**

**Answer to Question 4**

**(a) No**: copper is less reactive than iron.

**(b) Yes**: $\mathrm{Cu(s)}$ + $\mathrm{2AgNO_{3}(aq)}$ $\longrightarrow$ $\mathrm{Cu(NO_{3})_{2}(aq)}$ + $\mathrm{2Ag(s)}$; the solution turns blue. This is how silver is recovered.

items.prompt: A zinc granule is dropped into blue copper sulphate solution. Which gives the products and what you would see?
options: $\mathrm{ZnSO_{4} + Cu}$; the blue fades and brown copper coats the zinc
$\mathrm{ZnSO_{4} + Cu}$; the solution turns green and the zinc turns grey
no reaction; zinc is less reactive than copper
$\mathrm{Zn_{2}SO_{4} + Cu}$; the blue fades and brown copper coats the zinc

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**C**: magnesium is more reactive than iron, so it displaces iron. In the others, the free metal is less reactive.

**On Question 2**

$\mathrm{Zn(s)}$ + $\mathrm{CuSO_{4}(aq)}$ $\longrightarrow$ $\mathrm{ZnSO_{4}(aq)}$ + $\mathrm{Cu(s)}$. Zinc sulphate is colourless, so the blue fades; reddish-brown copper coats the zinc. **D** has the wrong formula for zinc sulphate.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• (a) Sodium sulphate solution poured into barium chloride solution.

• (b) Lead nitrate solution poured into potassium iodide solution.

**Answer to Question 5**

**Barium sulphate**; sodium chloride stays dissolved.

$\mathrm{Na_{2}SO_{4}(aq)}$ + $\mathrm{BaCl_{2}(aq)}$ $\longrightarrow$ $\mathrm{BaSO_{4}(s)}$ + $\mathrm{2NaCl(aq)}$

**What this shows**

Displacement: an element pushes another out of a compound. Double displacement: two compounds swap ions.

**Answer to Question 6**

**(a)** $\mathrm{Pb(NO_{3})_{2}(aq)}$ + $\mathrm{2KI(aq)}$ $\longrightarrow$ $\mathrm{PbI_{2}(s)}$ + $\mathrm{2KNO_{3}(aq)}$

**(b) Yes**: the ions swap partners. The yellow precipitate of lead iodide makes it a **precipitation** reaction too.

chunks.name: Copper gains oxygen, then loses it

items.text:
**What this shows**

• (a) Brown copper powder heated in a china dish.

• (b) Hydrogen passed over the hot black powder in a glass tube.

**Answer to Question 7**

**Oxygen**:

$\mathrm{2Cu}$ + $\mathrm{O_{2}}$ $\xrightarrow{\text{heat}}$ $\mathrm{2CuO}$ (black copper(II) oxide)

**Answer to Question 8**

**Oxygen**, which joins hydrogen to form water:

$\mathrm{CuO}$ + $\mathrm{H_{2}}$ $\xrightarrow{\text{heat}}$ $\mathrm{Cu}$ + $\mathrm{H_{2}O}$

**What this shows**

A substance that **gains oxygen** or **loses hydrogen** is **oxidised**; one that **loses oxygen** or **gains hydrogen** is **reduced**. One is oxidised while the other is reduced: a **redox reaction**.

The substance that gives oxygen or takes hydrogen is the **oxidising agent**; it is itself reduced. The one that takes oxygen or gives hydrogen is the **reducing agent**; it is itself oxidised.

items.prompt: In $\mathrm{2PbO + C  \longrightarrow  2Pb + CO_{2}}$, which statement is correct?
In $\mathrm{H_{2}S + Cl_{2}  \longrightarrow  2HCl + S}$, which statement is correct?
options: $\mathrm{H_{2}S}$ is oxidised; $\mathrm{Cl_{2}}$ is reduced and is the oxidising agent
$\mathrm{H_{2}S}$ is reduced; $\mathrm{Cl_{2}}$ is oxidised and is the oxidising agent
$\mathrm{H_{2}S}$ is oxidised; $\mathrm{Cl_{2}}$ is reduced and is the reducing agent
$\mathrm{Cl_{2}}$ is oxidised; $\mathrm{H_{2}S}$ is the oxidising agent

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**C**: $\mathrm{PbO}$ gives oxygen to carbon, and is itself reduced to lead.

**On Question 2**

$\mathrm{H_{2}S}$ loses hydrogen: **oxidised**. $\mathrm{Cl_{2}}$ gains hydrogen: **reduced**, so $\mathrm{Cl_{2}}$ is the **oxidising agent**.

items.text:
**Answer to Question 10**

The fats and oils in the namkeen were **oxidised** by the air, which changes their smell and taste. **Nitrogen is unreactive** and keeps oxygen away from the chips.

**Answer to Question 11**

**(i)** Double displacement and precipitation.

**(ii)** Combination and exothermic; magnesium gains oxygen, so it is **oxidised**.

A reaction can belong to **more than one type**: ask every question.
